files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: L. Mbeki. Complete in sequence. No shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months all payroll runs pay in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to prevent duplication. If the entry is missing, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL does not already contain the entry.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with GL coding. Verify each expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after obligations 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Harborline Supply Co. began when two former warehouse colleagues noticed that local businesses were spending too much time chasing routine supplies from several different distributors. They built the company around a straightforward promise: keep dependable stock on hand, answer the phone, and make deliveries when customers expect them.

The company wholesales workplace essentials, packing materials, light facility supplies, and general commercial goods to regional offices, retailers, service firms, and small industrial customers. Its business is deliberately practical. Customers tend to value consistent availability and familiar account support more than flashy catalogs or complicated programs.

The team has a hands-on character. Sales staff know the warehouse aisles, purchasing keeps close contact with regular vendors, and drivers often hear about a customer’s next order before it reaches the office. Inside the accounting group, month-end is handled with checklists, supporting documents, and a preference for resolving small discrepancies before they become recurring problems.

Harborline Supply Co. remains an ordinary going concern focused on serving its established customer base while improving product organization, delivery coordination, and vendor relationships. Current priorities include clearer inventory descriptions, steadier purchasing routines, and more useful communication between sales, operations, and finance.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Keep Harborline Supply Co. practical and recognizable: dependable stock, responsive people, and straightforward wholesale service. The refresh should feel cleaner, not corporate.

## Priorities

- Update core brand language across sales sheets, email templates, and customer-facing materials.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, centered on inventory planning, workplace supply readiness, and smoother ordering.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with a complementary regional vendor.
- Build short customer stories that show how reliable fulfillment helps day-to-day operations.
- Give the sales team reusable follow-up notes and simple campaign talking points.

## Quarter plan

### Q3

Finalize messaging, refresh the most-used materials, select webinar topics, and recruit a pilot partner. Reconnect with dormant accounts using service-led outreach rather than discount-heavy promotion.

### Q4

Expand the strongest webinar theme, publish customer stories, review partner-pilot results, and prepare recommendations for the next planning cycle.

## Measures to watch

Track webinar attendance, qualified follow-up conversations, reactivated accounts, partner-sourced inquiries, and use of refreshed materials by the sales team. Budget remains pending completion of the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# A few handoff notes

L. Mbeki — these are the things I would keep beside the close checklist:

- The bank usually puts its own fees and charges near the end of the statement. We do not book those during the month; pick them up at close.
- I moved quickly through June processing, so the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and correct the GL to match them.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. Any one-off items that arrived in June were not planned, and they are the reason some of the variances look large.
- For payroll, trust the register on the back-half run's pay date. In some months that run slips into the next month; do not assume the timing without checking.
